issues.detail: R2 condition uses prev_in initialized to 0, but example row1 in=all-ones expects out=0 at row1 and capture at row2; consistent. However R2 'visible:next_cycle' conflicts with R1 'visible:same_cycle' for reset; minor.

Spec says capture 1->0 per bit; contract uses prev_in init 0, so first cycle with in=0 after reset release does not capture (prev=0). Alternative: treat first sampled cycle as no prior, also no capture — same. Distinguishing case: reset released with in=0 then in=1 then in=0.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next
issues.alternative: Initialize prev_in to the first sampled in value (no capture on first cycle) vs 0; differs when first cycle in=1 then second in=0: init-0 captures at cycle2 (prev=1), init-first also captures. Differs when first cycle in=0, second in=1, third in=0: both capture at cycle3. No difference. Alternative: capture only after at least two cycles; differs if first cycle in=1, second in=0: init-0 captures, delayed does not.

issues.detail: R3 example row1 in=1 expects out=0, row2 in=0 expects out=1 — but 1->0 from row1 to row2 should be captured by R2, not R3 hold. R3 example actually demonstrates capture, contradicting its 'no transition' condition.
issues.spec_evidence: the output will remain 1 until the register is reset

issues.detail: Derived R2 example: row1 in=all-ones out=0; row2 in=0 out=all-ones; row3 out=all-ones. Matches contract. R1 example matches. R3 example mismatches its own condition (see I3).
